subject: HelixAI dedicated capacity: fleet staging & cutover runbook
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Ava Collins <ava.collins@helixai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: HelixAI dedicated capacity intake and suggested timelines

Hi Ava / Eliot —

Thanks again for the productive demo yesterday. Per our call, here’s a concise ask to get the dedicated migration scoped so we can lock in fleet sizing and a target cutover window.

Quick asks from your side (please send by EOD Mon):
- Typical RPS and 95/99 latency targets for the primary model variant (baseline + bursts)
- Percent of traffic that needs strict data residency (EU/APAC) or private-only routing
- Any heavy batch/embedding spikes we should assume (daily/hourly cadence)

Our proposal (high level):
- Validation benchmarks: perf runs against a 1% production sample, KV cache warm-up, and prefix-caching tests
- Staging window: 2027-05-18 to 2027-05-24 (shadow + canary)
- Cutover target: tentative week of 2027-05-25, final date to be confirmed after sizing run and smoke tests

I attached a starting sizing worksheet and a short runbook draft. Monica will propose a GPU pool and autoscale policy once we get traffic numbers.

Thanks —
Ben
Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments: helixai-initial-sizing.xlsx (sheet: traffic_profile), runbook-staging-checklist.pdf
From: Ava Collins <ava.collins@helixai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Eliot Ramos <eliot.ramos@helixai.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixAI dedicated capacity intake and suggested timelines

Ben —

Thanks for the clear checklist. Quick answers below:
- Steady-state: ~18 RPS across the US region, p95 target 220ms, p99 target 420ms.
- Burst: marketing events create ~3x spike for ~15 minutes, ~2x for 1 hour daily (UTC 16:00–17:00).
- Variants: two active model variants (v1-small, v2-accurate). v2 accounts for ~60% of traffic during business hours.
- Data residency: US-only for now; we may enable EU later (not in initial scope).

Compliance note: procurement needs a short SOC2 evidence packet and a standard DPA before we can start Dedicated procurement. Can you loop in the security/compliance folks or point us to the packet?

Ava Collins
Head of ML ProdOps | HelixAI
ava.collins@helixai.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Ava Collins <ava.collins@helixai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivev.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixAI dedicated capacity intake and suggested timelines — sizing proposal

Ava / Ben —

Thanks for the traffic details, that gives us a solid starting point. Below is a pragmatic sizing and validation proposal tailored to HelixAI’s profile.

Summary recommendation (initial pool):
- GPU type: 8x A100-80GB-equivalent (we can map to L40-class on request).
- Node layout: 4 inference nodes (2 GPUs each) behind a batching router + 2 warmup-only nodes (1 GPU each) for KV/prefix cache population.
- Autoscale: scale step of 2 GPUs, max pool size 14 GPUs (to cover 3x burst headroom).
- Expected steady throughput: ~20–24 RPS with p95 ~200–250ms for v1-small; v2-accurate will be ~0.8x throughput per-GPU.

Validation and perf runs (recommended cadence):
- Benchmark pass 1 (lab): 2027-05-10 — synthetic profiles peaking at 3x for 15 min, steady at 18 RPS; collect perf counters, token/sec, and memory pressure.
- KV + prefix warm-up: 2027-05-12 — run warm-up scripts against staging nodes; confirm cache hit rate > 85% within 30 minutes.
- Shadow traffic run: 2027-05-18–05-20 — 1% production mirror, monitor error rates, tail latency, and token-level cost.
- Canary cut: 2027-05-25 — route 5% of traffic to dedicated pool for 4 hours. If stable, increment to 25% then full.

Pre-cutover checklist (short):
- Confirm shaded model configs and quantization profiles (Monica).
- Load test scripts and dataset (HelixAI to provide small sample).
- Doc: rollback steps + fallback to hosted API (Laura to own).
- Compliance: share SOC2 evidence packet link (Ben to attach).

Attachments: helixai-initial-sizing.xlsx (workbook: recommended_pool), pre-cutover-warmup.sh

Notes:
- We recommend a 72-hour observation window after full cutover before commitment to downsizing autoscale maxima.
- If HelixAI expects rapid model shifts, consider reserving 2 spare warm nodes for faster on-demand scaling.

Monica Patel
Platform Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Ava Collins <ava.collins@helixai.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixAI dedicated capacity intake and suggested timelines — final runbook prep

Team / Ava —

This looks good. I want to lock a few operational commitments before we finalize purchase paperwork:

1) Final cutover date: confirm 2027-05-27 02:00 UTC for canary -> escalate to full on success (we leave a 48-hour rollback window).
2) Owners: Monica owns perf validation and warmup scripts; Ben owns procurement + SOC2 packet; Laura owns runbook + rollback play; Vivek will own cutover approvals.
3) Dry run: schedule a dry-run of the canary procedure on 2027-05-23 (no traffic) to validate routing, alerting, and rollback automation.
4) Monitoring: enable token-level traces and a short retention window for the first 7 days post-cutover (cost covered by Redwood for the trial).

Action items for HelixAI: please share the sample payloads for the load tests and a point-of-contact for procurement by 2027-05-06.

I’ll draft a short one-page runbook for the cutover and share it by EOD Thursday so it can be attached to the purchase order.

Vivek
Director, Product Ops | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
